template: Pet an animal (cannot be your own).
Change your hair.
Clean your whole house.

Go to the mall to buy an outfit.

Ask someone for a date.
Flirt with someone you might never see again.

Ride your bike for 30 minutes.

Go to the park.

Go out to dinner alone.
Go to a store and tip the cashier 25%.
Go to a coffee shop you've never been to and order a drink you've never tried.
Go to a thrift store and buy one item under $10 that you have to style an outfit around.

Go to a restaurant and sit at the bar or a table alone, no phone, and finish your entire meal just observing and thinking.
Take a different route home than usual, walking or driving, and stop to take a picture of the most interesting thing you notice.
Leave three anonymous positive notes (like You got this, Proud of you, etc.) in public places for strangers to find.
Ask a stranger whose style you like where they got one specific item they're wearing.
Go to a public place such as a mall, park, or plaza and record a short video about [topic] in one take, then post it without re-recording.

Attend a free community class or workshop in your city.
Text or call someone you haven't spoken to in at least 6 months.
Go to a museum or art gallery and spend at least 30 minutes with no phone out.
Cook a new recipe from scratch and plate it like you're serving a guest.
Ask a barista or server what their favorite item on the menu is and order it.
Go to the movies alone, watch a full film, and don't check your phone once.
Buy a small snack or drink and give it to someone working a thankless job such as a janitor, security guard, or cashier.
Sit in a busy public place and sketch what you see for 20 minutes, even if you feel like you can't draw.
Spend one evening with no social media and write one full page about how you actually feel about life right now.
Sign up for a local event or meetup and stay for at least 45 minutes.
Try a new type of physical activity such as a yoga class, boxing gym, or dance class at least once.
Write down 10 new ideas for businesses, projects, or songs in one sitting without judging them.
Take a night walk for at least 20 minutes and focus only on the sounds and lights around you.
Hold the door open for 5 people in a row and make eye contact with each one.
Learn a simple magic trick or bar trick and perform it for at least one person in real life.
Visit a local small business and buy one thing you don't normally buy.
Go a full day without social media and write a paragraph about how it felt.
Take public transportation such as a bus or train to somewhere you don't usually go and walk around for 30 minutes.
Donate at least one bag of clothes or items you don't use anymore.
Ask a family member to tell you a story from their childhood you've never heard before.
Try a new restaurant and order something you've never had before.
Sit outside at night for 20 minutes and just look at the sky with no phone.
Buy a greeting card and write a genuine note to someone you appreciate, then give or mail it.
Go to a public place and intentionally smile at 5 strangers.
Spend 1 hour rearranging or redesigning one corner of your living space to feel more like you.
Find a local scenic spot such as an overlook, park, or river and take 5 photos like you're doing a mini photoshoot.
Listen to an album you've never heard before from start to finish with no multitasking.
Ask someone older than you for one piece of life advice and write it down.
Go to a café or park and spend 30 minutes reading a physical book or magazine.
Try a new coffee, tea, or snack spot and leave a kind review online afterward.
Go to a grocery store and buy three fruits or snacks you've never tried before.
Sit in a café and write down 20 ideas for things you want to do before you die.
Ask a stranger for a restaurant recommendation and write it down, with bonus points if you actually go.
Wear an outfit that's slightly outside your normal style and go out in public for at least an hour.
Visit a playground at night if it's safe and sit on a swing for 10 minutes thinking about your younger self.
Write a handwritten letter to your future self and seal it to open in 1 year.
Walk into a hotel lobby like you belong there and sit for 15 minutes people-watching.
Buy a small plant and name it, then put it somewhere visible in your home.
Take a photo of yourself somewhere outside that makes you feel powerful or like the main character.
Go to a public place and strike up a short conversation with someone who is also alone.
Spend 30 minutes researching a country you've never thought about visiting and save 3 photos of it.
Do a solo album listening session in your room with the lights low, one album on, and no phone, just listening.
Go a full day saying yes to every reasonable invitation or opportunity that doesn't go against your values.
Find a local mural or interesting wall and take a creative self-timer photo in front of it.
Ask someone what their dream job or dream life looks like and really listen to their answer.
Walk into a high-end store you normally wouldn't and try on one thing with no obligation to buy.
Give a genuine, specific compliment to a man you don't know, and give a genuine, specific compliment to a woman you don't know, respectfully.
Spend 20 minutes organizing your phone: delete unused apps, change your wallpaper, and tidy your home screen.
Pick one fear or insecurity you have and talk about it out loud in a voice note just for yourself, then listen back once.
Write a one-page journal entry about [topic] and keep it somewhere you'll see again.
Voice-record a 60-second rant or love letter about [topic] and listen back once.
Go on a walk and think only about [topic] for 10 minutes, then write 5 bullet points about what came up.
Find a quote about [topic] online and send it to [person] with one sentence about why you chose it.
Call [person] and ask them for their honest opinion on [topic] without debating them.
Send a text to [person] telling them how they influenced your thinking about [topic].
Ask [person type], such as an older neighbor, coworker, or barista, how they feel about [topic] and write down their answer.
Write a private letter to [person] about [topic] and decide whether or not to send it later.
Make a 3 to 5 song playlist that feels like [topic] and share it with [person].
Ask [person type] who inspires you, such as a mentor, creative friend, or hustler friend, what [topic] means to them.
Draw or doodle a rough logo or symbol for [topic] and pin it where you'll see it daily.
Invite [person] to do a 10-minute brainstorm session with you about [topic], in person or on a call.
Record a selfie video explaining [topic] to your future self and save it in a special album.
Ask [person younger than you] how they think about [topic] and what they expect in 10 years.
Ask [person older than you] what they wish they knew earlier about [topic].
Write down three promises to yourself about [topic] and tell [person] so they can hold you to it.
Compliment a stranger and learn something about them.
Climb a tree.
Do 15 push ups.
Do a 10 minute bodyweight workout: squats, push ups, and lunges with minimal breaks.
Hold a wall sit for as long as you can, rest, then try to beat your time once more.
Hold a plank for as long as you can, rest, then do one more round.
Find a set of stairs and walk up and down for 10 minutes without using an elevator.
Do one grocery trip where you carry your bags by hand for at least 5 minutes without stopping.
Do 3 sets of 10 slow, controlled squats, focusing on form and balance.
Do a pushup ladder: 3 push ups, rest, 4 push ups, rest, keep adding 1 rep until you can’t complete a set.
Fill a backpack with books or items and go for a 15 minute walk wearing it.
Do 3 sets of 15 glute bridges, pausing for a second at the top of each rep.
Do 3 sets of 20 standing calf raises on a step or curb.
Pick up a safe, moderately heavy object from the floor with good form for 3 sets of 10 reps.
Use a sturdy doorframe or rail to do 3 sets of 8 to 12 bodyweight rows.
Stand on one leg and reach toward the floor 10 times, then switch legs and repeat.
Use dumbbells or filled water jugs for 3 rounds of curls, shoulder presses, and rows.
Do 5 burpees, rest, and repeat for a total of 5 rounds.
Sit down and stand up from a chair 25 times without using your hands.
Carry something heavy in each hand, like bags or weights, and walk for 2 minutes without setting them down.
Choose one pushing exercise and one pulling exercise and do 3 working sets of each.
Go for a 30 minute walk where you intentionally power walk hills or inclines when you find them.
Spend 10 minutes doing basic stretches, then 10 minutes doing strength moves like squats, lunges, and push ups.
Go to a grocery store and ask an employee what their favorite item is, then buy it and try it later.
Visit a local park and walk every main path until you've seen the whole park.
Sit in a café and write five things you appreciate about your current life in a notebook.
Text three different people and start a genuine non-surface level conversation with each.
Go somewhere busy and spend 10 minutes just listening to the sounds around you with no phone.
Spend 15 minutes stretching every major muscle group slowly and intentionally.
Record a one-minute video pep talk to your future self and save it privately.
Walk to a place you usually drive to and notice what you see differently along the way.
Go to a clothing store and try on an outfit that is completely outside your usual style.
Spend 20 minutes cleaning or organizing a small area you usually ignore.
Pick one creative idea you've been avoiding and work on it for 25 minutes with no distractions.
Go outside at sunrise or sunset and stand still for 10 minutes just watching the sky.
Invite [person] to join you for a walk or coffee and talk about something real.
Write down a fear you have, then list 10 small actions you could take related to it.
Go to a local community space such as a library, rec center, or church and stay for 20 minutes just observing.
Do a 10 minute walk where every time you see a new color, you name it out loud.
Ask [person] what they think your hidden strengths are and write down what they say.
Spend 15 minutes researching a skill you want to learn this year and write 5 first steps.
Put on a song that makes you feel powerful and dance full out until the song ends.
Go to a quiet place and meditate on your breath for 7 minutes, counting each exhale.
Buy a snack or drink for someone working a late or early shift and thank them for their work.
Write a list of 20 things you are curious about, no matter how random.
Spend 15 minutes intentionally tidying your appearance as if preparing for an important meeting.
Take a 25 minute walk where you think only about [topic] and no other subject.
Write 10 different possible futures for yourself in one sentence each.
Go somewhere with a mirror and practice holding eye contact with yourself for 3 minutes.
Journal freely for 15 minutes about why [topic] matters to you right now.
Ask [person] to tell you a story from their life you've never heard before.
Do a 5 minute cold exposure such as a cold shower or stepping outside underdressed, safely.
Find a staircase and go up and down it continuously for 12 minutes.
Spend 20 minutes without your phone in a public place, just noticing micro-interactions around you.
Write down 15 things you like about your current self, even if they feel small.
Clean out and reorganize one drawer, shelf, or digital folder completely.
Go to a store and ask for a genuine recommendation on a product, then consider buying it.
Invite [person] to share one thing they are struggling with and just listen without fixing.
Create a 3 song playlist for a specific mood and listen to it start to finish with no distractions.
Spend 20 minutes learning about a country, culture, or city you know almost nothing about.
Take a 30 minute walk where you avoid all your usual routes and turn a different way each time.
Draw a quick map of your life over the last 5 years and mark the turning points.
Choose one person you admire and study their story for 20 minutes, taking notes.
Spend 10 minutes practicing your posture and walk around like the confident version of you.
Go to a live event you find on short notice, such as a small show, talk, or open mic.
Ask [person] what they think your life will look like in 5 years and write their answer down.
Stand outside your home and look at it like a stranger, noticing all the details for 5 minutes.
Spend 15 minutes reviewing your recent photos and delete any that no longer feel like you.
Write a one page story about a version of you who already solved your biggest current problem.
Do a 20 minute home workout video you find online, completing it all the way through.
Spend 10 minutes talking out loud about your week as if you are on a podcast.
Buy or bring a flower and leave it in a public place with a kind note attached.
Take a 40 minute walk where you intentionally speed up on hills and slow down on flat parts.
Spend 25 minutes planning a mini adventure you could do within 2 hours of where you live.
Write down 10 limiting beliefs you have and one sentence arguing against each.
Choose a room and remove five items you no longer need, then put them in a donation bag.
Go sit somewhere you have never sat before in your own city and stay for 15 minutes.
Ask [person] to recommend a book, movie, or album and commit to trying it this month.
Do 3 rounds of 30 seconds fast walking or jogging, 30 seconds rest.
Write a short message to [person] appreciating something specific they did for you.
Spend 20 minutes designing your perfect slow morning in writing or sketching.
Take 15 minutes to stand or sit with a straight back, imagining a string lifting your head up.
Spend 25 minutes researching one habit you want to build and the science behind it.
Walk to a nearby store, buy one healthy item, and eat or drink it mindfully.
Sit on public transport and deliberately make eye contact and smile at three people.
Write a letter forgiving yourself for something in your past, then keep or discard it.
Spend 15 minutes standing or walking barefoot on grass or ground if possible.
Choose a building in your neighborhood and imagine the lives of three people who might live there.
Call [person] and tell them one memory with them that still makes you smile.
Take a 20 minute walk where you leave your headphones at home and listen to your thoughts.
Spend 10 minutes choosing an outfit for tomorrow that supports the version of you you want to be.
Find a local viewpoint, rooftop, or bridge and look over your city for 10 minutes.
Write down 30 things you have already survived or overcome.
Do a quick workout circuit of squats, push ups, and jumping jacks for a total of 10 minutes.

Write a one page scene where your life is a movie and today is the turning point.
Sit somewhere outdoors and list 25 things you can see, hear, smell, or feel.
Ask [person] for honest feedback on one habit or pattern you have and just listen.
Take a 15 minute walk where you say out loud one thing you are grateful for every minute.

Do a 20 minute tidy of all visible surfaces in one room so it feels lighter.

Write out your ideal day hour by hour from waking up to going to sleep.

Go outside for 10 minutes and intentionally say hi to at least three people.
Write 10 affirmations that actually sound like you and feel believable.

Walk a full loop around your block or building three times in a row.
Spend 20 minutes creating a moodboard for the next season of your life using images or sketches.

Go to a shop and ask someone working there how their day is going and really listen.

Take a 10 minute walk in the rain, snow, or less-than-perfect weather, safely dressed for it.
